recommendation: Keep the commit as-is; no further FHIR-core change is needed for FHIR-51486 unless a later WG decision changes DeviceAlert coding semantics. Do not fold FHIR-51936 into core because it belongs to HL7/fhir-extensions and was already applied there.
issue_request: FHIR-51486 asked the Devices WG to reconsider DeviceAlert code elements because primitive code cannot carry system or version; the Applied/Persuasive with Modification resolution left status unchanged and changed type, priority, signal.activationState, and signal.presence to CodeableConcept with extensible bindings.
initial_application: HL7/fhir#3695, merged as c0d69e61555228b39aeb4092cc5dfdcf564314a7 with implementation commit 819e689141ca71ac8a78ec920e55b6e1515b7d17, updated the DeviceAlert StructureDefinition and converted priority plus signal activation/presence in the example, but missed DeviceAlert.type in the example.
additional_context: DeviceAlert is active in source/fhir.ini. Zulip and Devices WG minutes show the issue was reopened after required-binding concerns and resolved to extensible bindings. The related Extension Pack issue FHIR-51936 was published separately for device-alertDetection.
reconciliation: Changed source/devicealert/devicealert-example.xml so DeviceAlert.type is a CodeableConcept coding from http://hl7.org/fhir/devicealert-type with code physiological/display Physiological.
source_changes: source/devicealert/devicealert-example.xml: changed DeviceAlert.type from <type value="physiological"/> to a CodeableConcept coding using http://hl7.org/fhir/devicealert-type#physiological.
